LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes of all time. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he rose to prominence as a high‑school phenom and was drafted first overall by the Cleveland Cavaliers in 2003. LeBron has played for the Cavaliers, Miami Heat, and Los Angeles Lakers, winning multiple NBA championships (2007, 2012, 2013, 2010, 2015, 2017, 2020) and earning numerous MVP awards.

Beyond the court, he’s known for his philanthropy—most notably the LeBron James Family Foundation, which opened the “I Promise School” for at‑risk children in Akron—and his ventures in entertainment, including producing films and television shows. His impact extends into social activism, where he has been vocal on issues such as racial justice and education reform.
